analysis_steps.goal: Radial profiles and spectral index map

method.value: Average in concentric ellipses with i=13 deg, PA=5 deg; alpha map from Band 6+7 mtmfs; median in ellipses

evidence.quote: These profiles were obtained by averaging the emission within concentric ellipses, projected with the inclination and PA of the disk

key_parameters.value: Band 3 profile from two 90 deg cones N and S

evidence.quote: the profile at this band is calculated using only two $90^{\circ}$ cones to the North and South

analysis_steps.goal: Fit multiwavelength visibilities with parametric model

method.value: Fit real part of deprojected visibilities with I=B(Td)(1-exp(-tau)); power-law Td, tau0 and beta base plus three asymmetric Gaussian rings

evidence.quote: we aim at fitting an analytical model of the radial intensity profile of the disk to the real part of the observed deprojected visibilities

key_parameters.value: 51 free parameters; 2000 bins; 200 walkers, 100,000 iterations; 5 frequencies

evidence.quote: We used 200 walkers and ran 100,000 iterations

assumptions.value: Geometrically thin, vertically isothermal, absorption opacity only, nu0=345 GHz, r0=10 au, axisymmetric

evidence.quote: we assume that the disk is geometrically thin and vertically isothermal

fitting.value: Affine-invariant ensemble MCMC; Gaussian priors on flux systematics (10% B7, 5% B6/B3), offsets (~5% of resolution), i=13±1, PA=5±5; flat priors elsewhere; beta limited to 0.2-3.1; ring width lower limit ~0.01 arcsec

evidence.quote: we set a flat prior that limits $\beta$ to be between 0.2 and 3.1 at all radii

validation.value: Residual images; chains converged; also tested four-ring model

evidence.quote: our model successfully reproduces the observations in great detail

findings_qualitative.value: Rings show increases in tau coupled with decreases in beta, indicating accumulations of large grains; gaps have ISM-like p.

evidence.quote: our model finds that the multiple rings in HD 169142 can only be explained with increases in $\tau$ coupled with substantial decreases in $\beta$.

findings_qualitative.value: Snowlines of main volatiles do not coincide with B1 and B2/3; planet-disk interaction favored.

evidence.quote: our multi-wavelength analysis indicates that at least the most prominent substructures in HD 169142 (B1 and B2/3) are not associated with snowlines.

claims.hypothesis: Rings are dust traps with large grain accumulation rather than just optical depth increases
claims.experiment: Joint visibility fit at 0.89, 1.3, 3 mm with tau0 and beta rings
claims.result: Rings have increased tau0 and decreased beta; amax ~1 cm in rings, flatter p
claims.finding: Rings trace accumulations of large particles, probably in pressure bumps

evidence.quote: We find that the multiple ring features of the disk are produced by annular accumulations of large particles

claims.hypothesis: Inner ring could host conditions for the streaming instability
claims.experiment: Fit of Sigma_d, amax and p with DSHARP opacities

evidence.quote: If confirmed, this inner ring would represent an ideal location to trigger the streaming instability

claims.hypothesis: Snowlines or MHD effects explain the rings
claims.experiment: Compared fitted temperature profile to snowline locations and MHD predictions
claims.result: Main snowlines are not at the rings; B4 may be near CO snowline
claims.finding: Planet-disk interaction is the most likely origin

evidence.quote: Overall, our results strongly support the planet origin scenario, in agreement with other recent studies on HD 169142.

why_this_method.value: Visibility-domain fitting avoids differing uv coverage and resolution among bands

evidence.quote: we perform our analysis in the visibility domain

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Four-ring model did not reproduce the triple outer ring; three-ring used

evidence.quote: our model with four rings does not reproduce the triple ring morphology of the outer disk

limitations_admitted.value: Finite resolution smears tau and beta; peak optical depths are lower limits

evidence.quote: the peak optical depths estimated by our model are in principle lower limits

limitations_admitted.value: Scattering neglected and dust composition assumed

evidence.quote: we have made the common assumption that the main source of opacity is the absorption opacity, without considering the scattering component

referee_caveats_inferred: Three free parameters per radius for two observables in the dust-size fit is degenerate
Results depend on assumed DSHARP composition and neglect scattering
